title: Wispr Flow Ads Strategy: 1,100 Live Meta Ads | Sprites
summary: How Wispr Flow runs 1,100 live Meta ads at a $2B valuation: the Trybe creator machine, the campaign naming, the funnel and the word-count paywall.
body_markdown:
Wispr Flow raised $280M at a $2B valuation on 17 August. Nine months earlier it was worth $700M. 60 billion words dictated, 10,000 enterprises, and a Notetaker launched the same week as the round.


Paid social is how they got there. 1,120 live Meta ads today, 4,180 ever. I read 819 of the live ones, measured 551 video files frame by frame, resolved every short link and walked the funnel from the ad to the paywall.


Two halves again: the Creative Factory, and the Performance Machine. This one has the biggest creative supply chain I have seen in consumer software.


## Wispr Flow ads: key findings


- **1,120** live Meta ads, **819** read
- **466** distinct video files behind 574 live video ads
- **52%** of live ads carry a Trybe creator ID in the URL
- **17** new ads a day over the last 60 days, **188** on the biggest day
- **27-second** median video, 96% vertical
- **65%** have a caption on screen at 0.3 seconds, sitting at 40% of frame height
- **494** distinct headlines across 819 live ads
- **19-day** median lifespan for ads that have ended
- The Notetaker took **85%** of September launches in the sample


16 of 551 Wispr Flow video files, sampled at 1.2 seconds. Collected 22 September 2026.


## Part 1: The Creative Factory


### 819 live ads, and 70% of them are video


Format Live ads read Share


Video 574 70%


Carousel 158 19%


Static image 87 11%


Behind the 574 video ads sit 466 files. 375 of them run as exactly one ad object. Viktor clones a winner twelve times. Wispr almost never clones, because a new file costs them almost nothing.


### 17 new ads a day


1,006 ads launched in the last 60 days. 188 of them on 21 August, four days after the round. 168 on 12 August. 103 on 15 September, the Notetaker.


The ones that end run a median of 19 days.


**They ship in waves, not a drip.** Three days account for 45% of two months of launches. Each wave is a batch of creator deliveries going live at once.


### Vertical, and shorter than you think


Median file is 27 seconds. 16% are under 15. The longest is six minutes 56 seconds, a creator's full video run as an ad.


529 of 551 files are 9:16. Eight are square, eight are landscape, six are 4:5. This is a phone account.


Video length Files

### The caption sits above the face


- 65% have a caption on screen by **0.3 seconds** . 71% by one second. 94% by six.
- Captions centre at **40% of frame height** . Above the eyes. A title card, not a subtitle.
- **Three words** a beat, at 3% of frame height. Small type, top of frame.
- **One cut** in six seconds, median. 39% have none.


Viktor's captions land at 58% of frame height, over the mouth, at 5% of the frame. Wispr's are smaller, higher and earlier. "POV: you quit typing." "Tech Luxury List." "Productivity hack for ADHD creators." The TikTok title card, unchanged, because the people who made these films make TikToks.


The hook is not a sentence somebody wrote for the brand. It is the sentence the creator would have used anyway.

The video account is 400 creators on their phones. The static account is warm, low light, serif type and a cream or forest-green card.


A woman at a desk at night, lit by the screen. "Backlog of unread messages you need to reply to?" A message bubble mockup with the ums struck out. "Meetings are full of words and names that notetakers get wrong" in italic serif on green. Every static is art directed and not one looks like a creator made it.


Same split as Viktor. The video says a person like you uses this. The static says a company you trust made it.

### 494 headlines. No positioning line.


819 live ads, 494 distinct headlines, 528 distinct body copies. The most common headline, "Names Right, Terms Right", is on 34 ads. The second, "Just speak. It writes.", on 32.


Viktor puts two headlines on 26% of the account and tests everything around them. Wispr writes a new headline for almost every ad, because the creator wrote the ad and the headline is their line.


What stays fixed is the claim inside the video. "4x faster than typing." "2x more accurate than Siri." "Zero edits." The creator says it in their own words, the brand never has to.


That is the other way to separate message from execution: hold the numbers, free the voice. ## Part 2: The Performance Machine


Now the half you cannot see in the feed.


### The campaign name is in the redirect


157 ads point at` ref.wispr.ai/meta` . Follow it and the landing page arrives with the campaign name attached:


` utm_campaign=S4_Evergreen_Scaling_Website_oAppDownload`


Field Value Meaning


Season S4 The fourth account structure. Three came before it.


Theme Evergreen Always-on, not a launch


Stage Scaling Past testing, budget goes up


Destination type Website Not the app store


Optimisation event oAppDownload The` o` prefix marks the event. Same convention as Viktor's` oStartTrial` .


The second short link,` ref.wispr.ai/meta-reset` , resolves to` utm_campaign=EvReset_PP` . An evergreen reset. Someone rebuilt the campaign and named the rebuild.


Every resolved link also carries a` dub_id` . Dub sits between the ad and the site, so a landing page can change without touching the ad object. Viktor does the same thing. So does everyone who has been burned by a learning-phase reset.


### Half the account is a creator ID


426 of 819 live ads carry` ?trybe=` and an eight-character hash. 342 distinct hashes. Trybe is a marketplace where creators shoot for brands and get paid on results: a fee per video, a commission on what the video converts, or both. The hash is the video's ID, and Trybe reads it server side to pay the creator.


It appeared in April 2026. 44 of that month's 94 launches carried it. By August it was 189 of 329.


Launch month Ads With a Trybe ID


March 2026 90 0


April 94 44


May 97 64


June 122 56


August 329 189


Their help centre says they are "not accepting new creator, sponsorship, or affiliate collaboration inquiries at this time." That is true. They do not need to. The marketplace does the recruiting, the brief, the delivery and the payout, and Wispr launches the file from its own ad account.


**This is the machine.** 342 live creator videos, each one paid on conversion, each one carrying its own ID. Viktor pays creators in credits. Wispr pays them a share of the download they caused.

Over the whole read, 55 more ads go straight to the Play Store or App Store, and 41 went to` wisprflow.ai/steven` .


The creator pages are the clever ones.` /steven` redirects to a page with` promo_code=STEVEN-BARTLETT` ,` utm_source=doac` ,` utm_medium=audio` and` utm_campaign=doac_flightcast_audio` .` /ali` resolves to` promo_code=ALI` ,` utm_medium=influencer` ,` utm_content=jan26_ytshort` . The short URL is what the creator says out loud. The long one is what the analyst reads.


And the YouTube ads resolve to` utm_campaign=yt_shanik` and` yt_baseline` . A creator's cut against a control, named as such.


### The road trip is an ad campaign


"Sveika Latvija, I need your help." A 52-year-old orange VW van, a host called Fabian, twelve countries, one video per country in the local language. Denmark and Norway are done, Poland is filming this week. Viewers vote on the next country's mission.


It has its own subdomain, its own Instagram, and seven live ads. It is the only thing in the account that is not a product demo.


### The funnel: sign in, download, then two permissions


**Step 1.** Four identity providers, or an email and a six-digit code. No password. On a phone, the same four buttons and the field.


1. **Sign in.** Google, Apple, Microsoft, SSO, or an email and "We sent a 6-digit code". No password anywhere.
2. **Download.** Mac, Windows, or the app store link the ad already sent you to.
3. **Two permissions.** Microphone, then Accessibility, which macOS makes you grant by hand in System Settings. The app walks you there.
4. **A mic test, a shortcut, a use case.** Push to talk or hands-free. Fn on a Mac. Then "what will you dictate?"


The Accessibility step is the real activation event. Until it is granted the product cannot type into anything, and the onboarding is built to get you through it.


**Note the referral disclosure.** "Your referrer will be able to see your email address once you sign up." Every signup page is also a referral landing page.

### 2,000 words a week, then $12


Free, Pro, Growth, Enterprise. The ROI calculator at the bottom does the selling.


Free is 2,000 words a week on desktop, 1,000 on iPhone, unlimited on Android. About 15 minutes of talking. Then the counter stops and Pro is $12 a user a month billed yearly, $15 monthly.


Plan Yearly Monthly


Free $0 $0


Pro $12 $15


Growth $18 $23


Growth with unlimited Notetaker $26 $33


Enterprise Custom


Inside the iPhone app the ladder is longer. $4.49 a week, $15 a month, $143.99 a year, and a student plan at $7.49. In India it is ₹400 a month, ₹320 yearly, paid by UPI.


No card at signup, no trial clock. The paywall is a word count, and the word count fires only after you have dictated 2,000 words into your own apps.


A usage wall is a wall you hit while using the thing. That is the only kind that converts on its own.


The pricing page ends with a calculator. Your hourly rate, in a box. "Time saved per month: 22 hours. Flow Pro monthly cost: $12. Estimated annual savings: $13,056." The number is theirs, the hourly rate is yours, and the page has done the arithmetic before you can.

### Investors, creators, a marketplace and a van


Four creator rails, none of them called a creator programme.


Rail How it pays Live ads


Trybe marketplace Fee per video and commission per conversion, by hash 426


Steven Bartlett Equity, plus a year-long Diary of a CEO partnership 41 over the read


Ali Abdaal Promo code and a YouTube Short 4


Come Flow With Me A van, a host, twelve countries 7


And for everyone else, the referral: a month of Pro when the friend you invited dictates 2,000 words. Not when they sign up. When they hit the same wall you did.


Which explains their other channels. 800 Google ads, and two thirds of the 777 I read are YouTube video, with "Get 'Voice-Pilled' With Flow" and "Siri vs. Wispr Flow" as headlines, a creator cut running against a baseline, and two creatives past 10 million impressions. 124 LinkedIn ads, 56 of them video, written as opinions: "Unexpected opinion: the most important job I've ever had was..." A brand that has learned to sound like a person.


## What actually makes this work


The Creative Factory is outsourced. 342 live creator videos from a marketplace, an investor with a podcast, a YouTuber with a promo code, and a van. Wispr shoots almost nothing. It brief, launches and pays.


The Performance Machine is what makes that affordable. The Trybe hash means every creator is paid on what they convert. The Dub redirect means every page can change without an ad reset. The word-count wall means the paywall only fires on people who already use the product.


Viktor built a factory and staffed it. Wispr built a marketplace and priced it.


Same result. 17 ads a day.
